name: partial_probe_and_diagnostics
status: EXPLORATORY. Written after every test set used here (TripClick TAIL, NQ, ArguAna) had been inspected for the paper; this is not independent confirmation. Frozen before any probe score, probe model or diagnostic category is computed on a test query. Every quantity below is reported regardless of outcome. If the probe analysis does not give reliable, interpretable results it is reported in the repository only.
question: Does observing part of an intervention (cross-encoder scores of the first k BM25 candidates) predict the benefit of full reranking better than pre-action telemetry, and does it pay for itself in total compute?
intervention: Cross-encoder reranking exactly as in the paper (MiniLM CONFIG.reranker_model over the BM25 top-100, reranked top-50 lead, BM25 order follows). Delta = the paper's stored reranking Delta per query.

probe.scores: Cross-encoder score of each of the first k BM25 candidates, same model and document text as the stored reranking run (scripts/48 rerank; ArguAna: scripts/52 with self-match exclusion already applied to the BM25 list). Audit: where the stored run has a score for the same document, the recomputed score must match to 1e-3.
probe.features: For probe size k: max, mean and std of the k scores; score of BM25 rank 1; max minus score of BM25 rank 1; position of the probe argmax in BM25 order; Spearman correlation between BM25 rank and probe score within the k; plus NQC over the BM25 top-100 (free) and query length: 9 features.
probe.on_skip: A query not selected for full reranking keeps its BM25 ranking (the probe's scores are paid for but not used to reorder).

models: scripts/54_baseline_runner.py cat_gbdt (the B1 form), unchanged, regressing Delta on the 9 probe features. Comparators: failure routing (TripClick/NQ: the paper's detector score; ArguAna: the registered runner failure router), NQC, B1 on the 10 pre-action features (TripClick: fit here under the same rule, local only; NQ: scripts/57 predictions; ArguAna: registered runner predictions), always, random, oracle.

data_use.tripclick_nq: Fit on the validation queries, ordered by sha256(qid + ':nq57'); first 70% train, rest selects hyperparameters (scripts/57 rule; for TripClick the same rule on TripClick validation). Scored once on test.
data_use.arguana: Registered split: fit on train, select on validation, score on test.

cost.unit: Measured wall-clock seconds per query on this machine.
cost.measurement: On 50 validation queries per corpus (sha256 order), time document-text fetch plus cross-encoder scoring for k pairs (k in probe sizes), for the remaining 100-k pairs, and for all 100; pipelines batched separately in alternating order, median per query. Pre-action telemetry cost for failure and B1 routing: measured likewise for the 8 t0 features on 50 validation queries (ArguAna: docs/arguana_feature_latency.txt). NQC and BM25 are charged to every policy equally and excluded.
cost.policy_cost: probe routing at full-rerank fraction b: probe(k) + b * remaining(100-k). Pre-action routing: telemetry (failure, B1; 0 for NQC) + b * full(100). Always: full(100).

analyses.primary: Per corpus, probe-10 routing minus failure routing and minus B1 routing in nDCG@10 gain, averaged over full-rerank fractions 10-75% (100% is shared), runner bootstrap_pair, 10^4 resamples, Holm over the 6 (3 corpora x 2).
analyses.cost_frontier: Gain versus mean seconds per query for every policy and budget; report, at each pre-action policy's points, the probe policy's gain at equal or lower cost (linear interpolation between its budget points).
secondary: benefit prediction quality on test: Spearman(predicted, Delta) and AUC for helped (Delta > 0) for probe models vs B1 vs failure score
fraction fully reranked and oracle regret at each budget
harm rate among fully reranked queries

diagnostics.settings: All six TripClick/NQ BM25 settings of Table 3 and the three ArguAna interventions, existing traces only, no fitting.
diagnostics.categories: Prespecified Delta categories: rescue (F=1, Delta>0); failing unchanged (F=1, Delta=0); healthy large gain (Delta>=0.10); healthy small gain (0<Delta<0.10); healthy unchanged (Delta=0); small harm (-0.10<Delta<0); large harm (Delta<=-0.10). Thresholds are the paper's existing 0.10 effect threshold.
diagnostics.reported: Composition of the queries selected by failure routing, benefit routing (B1 where available) and the oracle at a 25% budget; share of oracle gain in each category; fraction of selected queries with Delta=0 (intervention inactive). Query examples only from public benchmarks (NQ, ArguAna), never TripClick.

outputs: docs/partial_probe_summary.json and docs/selection_diagnostics.json (rounded aggregates). Probe scores, predictions and per-query outputs stay in results/ (gitignored).
